Timeline::eq¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Timeline::eq(const Timeline& other) -> Series

What It Does¶

Performs elementwise temporal equality and returns a boolean Series.

This page is also the canonical reference for the sibling comparison methods:

  • ne

  • lt

  • le

  • gt

  • ge

All six methods share the same shape and broadcast contract. The only thing that changes is the comparison relation.

Parameters¶

other

The timeline to compare against.

This may be the same shape as self, or a scalar/broadcastable timeline when the comparison is conceptually “compare every element to one timestamp”.

Missing timestamps participate conservatively: a missing time does not compare as less-than or greater-than any real timestamp.

Returns¶

Series A boolean series describing the comparison result element by element.

Examples¶

Example 1. Equality keeps only rows where the timestamps match exactly.

auto out = base.eq(other);
std::cout << pluss::print_series(out) << "\n";

Output¶

Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[true, false, false, false]

Example 2. Less-than and greater-than comparisons answer true temporal ordering questions.

auto earlier = base.lt(other);
auto later_or_equal = base.ge(other);
std::cout << pluss::print_series(earlier) << "\n";
std::cout << pluss::print_series(later_or_equal) << "\n";

Output¶

base.lt(other):

Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[false, true, false, true]

base.ge(other):

Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[true, false, true, false]

Related Methods¶

  • ne(other) True where timestamps differ.

  • lt(other) True where self < other.

  • le(other) True where self <= other.

  • gt(other) True where self > other.

  • ge(other) True where self >= other.

Notes¶

  • Comparison methods are usually the front door into mask-based temporal logic.

  • Pair them with where when you want a temporal branch.

  • Pair them with DataFrame or Thread filtering when the timeline lives in a table column.
